macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Oil spikes on renewed Middle East tensions, lifting inflation worries
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil prices rose after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran, with Brent and other benchmarks firming as investors reassessed the risk of wider supply disruptions and higher inflation. The move also supported the U.S. dollar and pressured bonds and rate-sensitive assets.

items.title: Wall Street futures and global stocks steady after geopolitical shock
items.summary: Reuters said U.S. stock index futures edged higher as markets stabilized after the latest escalation in the Iran conflict, while European shares rose in choppy trading led by technology. Asian shares also gained, though the rally was limited by the jump in oil prices and renewed inflation fears.

items.title: Fed outlook turns more uncertain as oil and inflation signals conflict
items.summary: CNN reported that the Federal Reserve is facing a difficult policy backdrop: June CPI showed cooling inflation, but the recent surge in energy prices has revived concerns about future inflation pressure. The report said investors are unsure whether the Fed will hold rates steady again or face renewed pressure to tighten policy.

items.title: IMF warns inflation risk remains elevated in the global economy
items.summary: Financial Times coverage highlighted IMF concerns that inflation threats remain significant globally, with some Fed officials also still seeing the need for future rate hikes if price pressures persist. The backdrop suggests central banks are not yet fully confident that inflation has been defeated.

items.title: Markets monitor Fed caution as oil-price rebound hits Asia-Pacific stocks
items.summary: MarketScreener noted that Australian shares wobbled as caution around the Fed offset optimism from softer oil prices, while Japan’s Topix and Nikkei were mixed and the yen remained under pressure near multi-decade lows. The roundup also showed strength in Samsung Electronics and several commodity-linked markets.

items.title: PepsiCo beats revenue expectations, but demand remains uneven
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that PepsiCo posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the second quarter, despite softer North American demand as consumers pulled back spending. CNBC also flagged PepsiCo among the biggest premarket movers after a mixed earnings update.

items.title: Travel stocks and airlines under pressure as oil jumps
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that travel stocks fell and United Airlines dropped after the renewed rise in crude prices tied to the Iran conflict. Higher fuel costs are again becoming a direct market concern for transport and consumer-facing companies.

items.title: US market narrative shifts back to inflation after energy shock
items.summary: Reuters and CNN both pointed to a renewed market focus on inflation after oil’s sharp move higher, with investors reassessing the likelihood of further central bank tightening. That shift has become the dominant macro theme in the last 24 hours.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds toward $65K as risk appetite improves
items.summary: Bitcoin rose to around $65,000 after markets reacted to easing U.S.-Iran tensions, with traders also noting renewed institutional support and higher trading volume. Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin also posted gains in the same move higher.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly reclaims $66K before pulling back
items.summary: Crypto markets saw another volatile session, with Bitcoin briefly touching $66,000 before slipping back below $65,000 amid broader macro uncertainty. The report also highlighted a rebound attempt after renewed Middle East tensions eased.

items.title: XRP gains as SWIFT expands blockchain payments testing
items.summary: XRP rose after reporting linked SWIFT activity suggested broader adoption of blockchain-based payments among bank partners. The development adds to ongoing speculation about institutional use cases for Ripple-associated infrastructure.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong regulators moved to require crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication, signaling a stronger security posture for digital asset services in the region. The change is part of a broader compliance push affecting exchange operations.

items.title: CLARITY Act advances in the Senate amid crypto market structure debate
items.summary: The U.S. Senate advanced a portion of the CLARITY Act, pushing the crypto market structure bill one step forward while leaving additional political hurdles ahead. The vote underscores ongoing debate over how digital assets should be regulated in the United States.

items.title: Paul Grewal exits Coinbase legal leadership ahead of key policy vote
items.summary: Coinbase’s legal chief reportedly stepped down just before a crucial CLARITY vote, highlighting the importance of the coming regulatory fight for major U.S. crypto firms. The move comes as lawmakers continue to debate the future of crypto oversight.

items.title: Circle acquires nearly 1,000 blockchain patents from IBM
items.summary: Circle expanded its intellectual property portfolio by purchasing nearly 1,000 blockchain-related patents from IBM. The deal covers blockchain technology, banking, insurance, and cloud security, though the price was not disclosed.

items.title: Strategy sells $544.5M in stock without buying more Bitcoin
items.summary: Strategy raised $544.5 million through an MSTR sale but did not add to its Bitcoin holdings in the period covered. The update reflects a more cautious capital allocation posture even as institutional crypto interest remains elevated.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation cuts budget and staff in major restructuring
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation said it will reduce its budget by 40% and its headcount by 20% as part of a shift toward an endowment-style model. The move is one of the most significant project-governance developments in the Ethereum ecosystem this cycle.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across applications and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools. The release intensifies competition with Anthropic, Microsoft, and other vendors targeting enterprise automation.

items.title: Meta opens developer preview of Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded AI model positioned for multimodal reasoning and business use. The move puts Meta more directly into competition with paid AI model offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live, new real-time voice models
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The launch adds to the company’s multimodal product lineup and signals continued focus on interactive, voice-first AI.

items.title: xAI releases Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, which it described as its most intelligent model so far and aimed at coding plus agent-style workflows. The release highlights the rapid pace of frontier-model updates among major AI labs.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip manufacturing starting in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September. The effort is part of a broader infrastructure push to expand computing capacity for its AI systems.

items.title: Meta announces major Alberta data center buildout
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to support growing AI compute needs. The move reflects a wider industry trend of massive infrastructure expansion to power training and inference demand.

items.title: Micron commits more than $250 billion to U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest over $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging AI-driven demand for memory chips. The announcement underscores how the AI boom is reshaping semiconductor capex and domestic manufacturing plans.

items.title: China moves to tighten control over AI technology access
items.summary: Reuters reported that China is working to build a more closed ecosystem around its AI technology, including open-source models, as the U.S. increases restrictions on foreign access to advanced AI systems. The development adds to ongoing geopolitical fragmentation in the AI sector.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some smartphone and electronics parts
items.summary: India removed import duties on selected parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting existing 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower input costs for companies including Apple and Xiaomi and support domestic electronics manufacturing.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks
items.summary: Global financial messaging network Swift launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with an initial group of 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC. Swift says the system is designed to enable round-the-clock payments and compete with stablecoin-based alternatives.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion under new Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple said it plans to spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. The deal also includes Broadcom expanding a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans in-house manufacturing of an AI chip starting in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip from September, according to an internal memo. The company is pushing to expand computing power as it builds out its infrastructure.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules to detect and remove child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed a proposal to reinstate temporary rules allowing Google, Meta, and other platforms to detect and remove online child sexual abuse material. The measure would extend platform scanning powers under a renewed regulatory framework.

items.title: MFE-MediaForEurope plans single streaming platform across European markets
items.summary: MFE-MediaForEurope said it plans to launch one streaming platform across its European markets by combining technologies developed by its Italian and German businesses. The broadcaster is stepping up competition with global digital and advertising rivals.
